I read pp. 25–27 and 144–148 and the Lean. For fixed d, Λ₀ and open Ω, exists_common_joint_analytic_profiles gives every Λ ≥ Λ₀ and C ≥ exp(Λ sup Re∫ζ*) a CoefficientProfile carrying: (4.13)/(B.15) cleared of the φ-denominator on |ΛX|<20 with f>0 on 0≤ΛX≤4.1; the form (B.12); Φ(0)=1, u(0)=0; the all-order bound (B.13) against f0(Yχ) and −YZ*/(2L), constants depending only on d; joint real analyticity. Data match (B.1)–(B.3). The three differences (F=φ/C normalization, scaled-only bounds, complex tube stated generically in AxisHolomorphic) are each recovered routinely. The pairing skeptic's correction stands: the headline is unused downstream; the main path uses exists_coefficientProfile.

findings.summary: Lean's angular profile is f = (φ*/C)·Φ(ΛX,η), the paper's F = φ/C of (4.4), not φ = φ*Φ. The equations are degree-one homogeneous in φ and Π_X = f² = φ²/C², so φ = C·f recovers the paper's form.
No declaration states the unscaled bound C_{r,s}Λ^{r−1}; Lean bounds only scaled Y-derivatives. Recovery: ∂_X^r[Ψ(ΛX,η)] = Λ^r(∂_Y^rΨ)(ΛX,η), so the C_{r,s}/Λ bound becomes C_{r,s}Λ^{r−1}.

The headline gives real joint analyticity on a fixed real Ω, not the Λ,C-uniform complex parameter tube. The tube is AxisHolomorphic.exists_common_holomorphic_extension (δ, bounds chosen before A) applied to F.coefficients, whose (B.4)-norm ball has fixed ε.
